# Prepare and import the data

This notebook is the portable analytical reconstruction of the current main
Figure 2 and the approved Supplementary Figure S2 (panels a–i). All paths used during a normal knit are relative to this folder. The
small analysis-ready objects, cached phylogeny, alignments, manifests and
reference artwork are stored locally so that the project can be moved to a
different computer without editing absolute paths.

The original normalized pan-mammalian beta matrix is approximately 3.9 GB. It
is not needed to reproduce the displayed correlations and is therefore not
duplicated here. Instead, the bundle contains the complete 37,554-probe
tissue-level correlation objects consumed by panels h, j and k, together with
the filtered sample annotation and sequence-alignment table. The raw source is
recorded in the provenance manifest for optional audit. For S2, a compact
sample-level extract of cg10501210 is also included: the human bootstrap
intervals can be recalculated without the full beta matrix.

Open `Figure2_main.Rproj` in RStudio, then Knit this document, or run
`source("render_figure2_and_s2.R")`. To build the plots without knitting, use
`source("run_figure2_and_s2_in_RStudio.R")`. To inspect saved plots immediately,
use `load("figures/supplementary_s2/Figure2_and_S2_workspace.RData")`.

## Upstream small-RNA processing

Eight animal datasets were reprocessed from raw reads with nf-core/smrnaseq 2.4.1. Mouse, rat and macaque instead used published expression matrices. The [dataset and run-settings inventory](data/miRNA_phylogeny/smallRNA_reprocessing_settings.tsv) records accessions, tissues, reference assemblies, adapter and read-length parameters. Mature counts were exported through EDGER_QC from the Bowtie/SAMtools branch. The local patch disabled downstream mirtop; those outputs were not used. Species-specific miRBase FASTAs were downloaded in May 2026. N. furzeri used the [NFINgb](https://nfingb.leibniz-fli.de/) genome and matching miRNA annotation, with strand-aware sequence extraction and header normalization that left mature sequences unchanged. The notebook starts from the resulting analysis-ready inputs and does not rerun raw-read processing.

## Load packages and reconstruct the analytical panels

```{r run-analysis-modules, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
required_packages <- c(
  "ape", "cowplot", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "gghalves", "ggrepel",
  "ggrastr", "ggtree", "ggtext", "grid", "knitr", "purrr", "readr", "ragg",
  "scales", "stringr", "svglite", "tibble", "tidyr"
)

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages)) {
  stop(
    "Install the following R packages before knitting: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Keep plotting environments independent of knitr's HTML-render state. This
# avoids serializing the whole rendered notebook into each reusable plot.
main_analysis_env <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
source("code/figure2_mirna_phylogeny.R", local = main_analysis_env)
source("code/figure2_methylation.R", local = main_analysis_env)
list2env(as.list(main_analysis_env, all.names = TRUE), envir = knitr::knit_global())

figure2_plot_objects <- list(
  panel_a = panel_a_tree,
  panel_f = panel_f,
  panel_g = panel_g,
  panel_h = panel_h,
  panel_i = panel_i,
  panel_j = panel_j,
  panel_k = panel_k
)

dir.create("figures/generated", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists("figures/generated/figure2_plot_objects.rds")) {
  saveRDS(
    figure2_plot_objects,
    "figures/generated/figure2_plot_objects.rds",
    compress = "gzip"
  )
}
if (!file.exists("figures/generated/figure2_workspace.RData")) {
  save(
    panel_a_tree, panel_f, panel_g, panel_h, panel_i, panel_j, panel_k,
    figure2_mirna_checks, figure2_methylation_checks,
    file = "figures/generated/figure2_workspace.RData",
    compress = "gzip"
  )
}
```

# Panel b - Cross-species miR-29 locus alignment

Panel b was generated with dedicated alignment software outside R and then
assembled in Illustrator. The complete final panel is represented here, while
the underlying alignment/provenance files are retained in
`data/manual_and_alignment/`. It is intentionally not presented as an R
recalculation.

The sequence catalogue in Supplementary Data 2 covers the 59 displayed
vertebrate species: 121 clusters containing 257 precursor loci, plus nine
singletons (266 loci in total). Each mature sequence is contained in its
corresponding precursor fragment. Assembly and nucleotide accessions,
chromosome/scaffold, strand and separate precursor and mature coordinates
are provided in the [locus catalogue](data/sequence_catalog/miR29_loci_and_sequences.tsv).
Coordinates are 1-based and inclusive; precursor-fragment boundaries denote
the extracted sequence around the mature miRNA, not experimentally mapped
processing boundaries. Sequence matches were determined in both orientations
on the designated reference chromosome or scaffold. Figure 2b remains an
illustrative alignment; use the catalogue and accompanying FASTAs for
sequence-level reuse.

```{r panel-b-reference, echo=FALSE, out.width='48%', fig.cap="Panel b. Cross-species alignment of host-gene, mature-3p and paralogue regions; imported manuscript artwork."}
knitr::include_graphics("reference/panel_b_reference.png")
```

# Panel f - Mature-miRNA associations with age

Panel f places the distribution of all measured mature-miRNA age correlations
in each species against the corresponding miR-29 family coefficients. The
analysis uses Spearman correlations. *Capra hircus* sample `SRR9663090` is
corrected from 24 days to 1 day, and *Macaca mulatta* is restricted to the 14

# Panel g - AGCACCA seed meta-analysis

Mature miRNAs are first collapsed by seed within species in Fisher-z space.
Species are then equally weighted within their macroclade, and the five
macroclades are equally weighted in the final vertebrate summary. Human is
excluded from this current panel; the corrected goat and brain-only macaque
inputs are retained.

## Draw panel g

```{r panel-g, fig.width=4.2, fig.height=5.4, fig.cap="Panel g. Equal-macroclade mature-miRNA seed meta-analysis excluding Human."}
panel_g
```

The locked AGCACCA result is rho = 0.8923, rank 1 of 76 tested seeds, with
1,385 profiles from 10 species.

# Pan-mammalian DNA-methylation analysis

The methylation panels use one locked hierarchy throughout:

1. Spearman correlation between probe beta and chronological age within each
   eligible species-tissue stratum;
2. unweighted arithmetic mean of tissue rho values within species;
3. equal-unit Fisher-z averaging above species, including the five-clade
   Boreoeutheria aggregate.

Samples require a recorded age and `Confidenceinageestimate > 80`. A
species–tissue stratum requires at least 10 retained samples; at least one
eligible tissue suffices for a species, and age-association plots require an
estimable target coefficient. The retained probe universe contains 37,554
mammalian-array probes. Species-level sample and tissue counts are reported
in Supplementary Data 2. The 36 conserved-target species in the five-clade
aggregate are a subset of the wider sequence survey, not all species that
pass the tissue filter.

# Panel h - Human CpG-age correlation atlas

The Human distribution includes all 37,554 probe-level tissue-balanced age
correlations. `cg10501210`, located in the regulatory region associated with
`MIR29B2CHG`, is the most negatively age-associated probe.

```{r panel-h, fig.width=4.8, fig.height=5.0, fig.cap="Panel h. Human tissue-balanced CpG-age correlation distribution with cg10501210 highlighted."}
panel_h
```

Locked result: rho = -0.5091, rank 1 of 37,554, across 1,126 filtered Human
profiles.

# Panel i - Conservation of the cg10501210 sequence

The portable alignment table reconstructs the analytical sequence matrix and
marks whether the target CpG dinucleotide is intact. Species ordering and
sequence calls are data-derived; animal silhouettes and the final curved probe
annotation remain editorial artwork.

For the illustrative alignment, 60 genomic fragments were uploaded to
[NGPhylogeny.fr](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkz303) in PhyML-SMS/OneClick
mode. MAFFT v7.467 (L-INS-i) aligned the sequences, followed by BMGE trimming.
The displayed alignment is the BMGE cleaned FASTA (step 7), shown in
MSAViewer with the nucleotide colour scheme; it is not the inferred PhyML
tree. The retained output has 60 sequences and 119 alignment columns.
The [genomic-fragment catalogue](data/sequence_catalog/cg10501210_conservation.tsv)
and [FASTA](data/sequence_catalog/cg10501210_60_genomic_fragments_DNA.fasta)
provide the final sequence records and assembly-specific coordinates for
sequence-level reuse, independently of the illustrative artwork.

The survey comprises 77 species with eligible tissues. The target CpG is
conserved in 41 and non-conserved in 25: 19 retain an alignable region with
a disrupted target dinucleotide, whereas six have an available reference
genome but no identified homologous probe-target region. Eleven species
are not assessable because the exact-species reference genome was
unavailable or inadequate and are excluded from the conserved/non-conserved
comparison. Thus the 60 available fragments represent 41 conserved and 19
non-conserved targets; their number does not arise from a requirement for
multiple tissues. The analysis uses *Sus scrofa* and does not pool the
separately labelled *Sus scrofa domesticus* samples.

## S2a — Locus-resolved miR-29 complement

Species follow the main radial phylogeny counterclockwise, from *C. milii* to
*H. sapiens*. Rows represent two positions in each of three clusters and a
separate singleton locus; the dot colour specifies the miRNA identity at that
position. Thus miR-29a replaces miR-29c within cluster I rather than occupying
an additional row. The green amphibian points in cluster I denote beta-2;
beta-1 is in cluster III of the three indicated teleosts. Small black centres
mark the annotated duplications. Empty positions indicate no annotated member
in the supplied reconstruction, not proof of biological absence.

The host-gene labels identify the corresponding human loci; they should not be
read as evidence that the same host-transcript annotation is conserved in
every species. The source table is the curated evolutionary reconstruction,
not an inference from the age-association datasets.

Cluster I–III, row identities and singleton assignments follow this panel.
The [species summary](data/sequence_catalog/miR29_species_and_clusters.tsv)
reports the number and composition of clusters and singletons. Within a
cluster, loci are ordered from the first miR-29b in the 5′-to-3′ direction,
accounting for strand. For b–c–b–c or b–c–c arrangements, the more distal
repeated locus receives the second copy index. This distinguishes separate
genomic copies even when their precursor sequences are identical. The
catalogue contains 15 additional intracluster copies, without overlapping
precursor fragments within a cluster. The source-tree outgroup
*Saccoglossus kowalevskii* is not one of the 59 displayed vertebrates.

```{r s2a-complement, fig.width=9.0, fig.height=2.9, fig.cap="S2a. Cluster- and locus-resolved miR-29 family complement, ordered as in the main phylogeny."}
p_S2a
```

## S2f–g — Target sequence status

These panels use the wider mapped sequence-status comparison, not only the
36 species entering main K. They compare 41 species with a conserved target
CpG and 25 with a non-conserved target, including both disrupted target
dinucleotides and absent homologous probe-target regions. The 11
not-assessable species are excluded. Supplementary Data 2 distinguishes
these sequence contexts and gives the available genomic fragments.

For f, normalized cg10501210 beta values are summarized within tissue and then
across tissues with equal tissue weight, yielding one point per species.
For g, species-level effects are arithmetic means of the eligible tissue
Spearman coefficients, consistently with the main methylation analysis.
Dot size in g represents sample coverage. Violin and box distributions
describe differences between species; they are not confidence intervals.

The beta comparison is an assay/sequence-status control: altered hybridization
or absence of the interrogated CpG can affect the signal. Low beta values in
the non-conserved group must not be interpreted as a direct measure of biological
hypomethylation at a conserved target. These comparisons are descriptive and
do not correct for phylogenetic non-independence.

```{r s2f-sequence-beta, fig.width=1.45, fig.height=1.70, out.width='32%', fig.cap="S2f. Species-level beta signal grouped by mapped target-CpG status."}
p_S2f
```

```{r s2g-sequence-rho, fig.width=2.25, fig.height=1.70, out.width='49%', fig.cap="S2g. Species-level cg10501210 age associations grouped by mapped target-CpG status."}
p_S2g
```

## S2h — Human tissue effects and bootstrap confidence intervals

The 13 estimable tissues are alphabetical, with the aggregate at the bottom.
The point estimate is the sample-level Spearman correlation of age with the
normalized cg10501210 beta signal within that tissue. Samples are resampled
with replacement **within tissue**, preserving each age–beta pair and the
original sample size. Spearman rho is recalculated in each of 2,000 draws
using seed 290105. The endpoints are the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles
(`quantile(type = 6)`), not symmetric standard-error bars. Thus a point need
not be centred between its two endpoints. Point area increases with sample
coverage and is not an inverse-variance weight.

The yellow diamond marks the **unweighted arithmetic mean of the 13 tissue
rho values**, not a random-effects meta-analysis. The aggregate interval is
obtained by taking that mean within each bootstrap iteration and then its
percentiles. It is conditional on these 13 tissues, does not resample tissues,
and does not account for cross-tissue donor dependence. We therefore do not
call it a donor-clustered or random-effects interval. The diamond itself has
a fixed graphical size; the horizontal whisker reports its interval.

```{r s2h-human-forest, fig.width=1.575, fig.height=1.417, out.width='45%', fig.cap="S2h. Alphabetical human tissue effects with sample-bootstrap 95% intervals; the bottom diamond is the arithmetic tissue aggregate."}
p_S2h
```

```{r s2h-ci-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(s2_hi_data$human_display[, c("label", "n_complete", "rho_cached", "ci_low", "ci_high")],
             digits = 4, caption = "Exact points and interval endpoints for S2h.")
```

## S2i — Leave-one-species-out and leave-one-clade-out

Each lower-panel point is the rebuilt global K coefficient after omitting
one species; its line connects it to the complete-analysis baseline
(`rho = -0.617636318578119`). These lines are changes relative to baseline,
**not confidence intervals**. All 37,554 probes are reaggregated and reranked
for each omission; the rank is not calculated using only cg10501210.

The hierarchy remains the one used in main K: arithmetic averaging across
tissues within species, Fisher-z averaging above species, with *Myotis* and
*Tursiops* retained as balanced genus-level units. If one of their species is
omitted, the genus unit is rebuilt from the remaining members. Five
macroclades receive equal weight in the full aggregate; after omitting a
clade, the four remaining macroclades receive equal weight.

The compact top strip reports the global coefficient and ascending global
rank after omitting each macroclade. Rank 1 means the most negative
coefficient. The target retains global rank 1 in all 36 species omissions;
clade omissions give ranks 1, 1, 1, 2 and 2. The full source table also retains
the target's within-clade rank after each species omission, which is a
different quantity and should not be confused with its global rank.

```{r s2i-omissions, fig.width=3.307, fig.height=1.929, out.width='95%', fig.cap="S2i. Compact clade-omission summary above species-omission effects. The dashed line is the full main-K baseline."}
p_S2i
```

```{r s2i-rank-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(s2_hi_data$clade_display[, c("omitted", "global_rho", "global_rank_ascending_min")],
             digits = 4, caption = "Leave-one-clade-out global results; the rank universe contains 37,554 CpGs.")
```

# Sequence catalogue and alignment references

The machine-readable sequence catalogue corresponds to the sequence and
cluster sheets of Supplementary Data 2:

- [Species and clusters](data/sequence_catalog/miR29_species_and_clusters.tsv)
- [Loci, precursor and mature sequences](data/sequence_catalog/miR29_loci_and_sequences.tsv)
- [All 266 precursor fragments, DNA FASTA](data/sequence_catalog/miR29_precursors_266_DNA.fasta)
- [The 257 clustered precursor fragments, DNA FASTA](data/sequence_catalog/miR29_clustered_precursors_257_DNA.fasta)
- [All 266 mature sequences, RNA FASTA](data/sequence_catalog/miR29_mature_266_RNA.fasta)
- [CpG conservation and genomic coordinates](data/sequence_catalog/cg10501210_conservation.tsv)
- [The 60 cg10501210 genomic fragments, DNA FASTA](data/sequence_catalog/cg10501210_60_genomic_fragments_DNA.fasta)

RNA sequences are written 5′ to 3′, and the seed is nucleotides 2–8 of the
recorded mature sequence. Genomic coordinates use the reference sequence's
forward-coordinate system and a separate strand field. The CpG-coordinate
columns describe the entire supplied fragment, not the individual CpG.
The catalogue preserves species labels used by each analysis; genome
annotations from a different species are not substituted for missing loci.

The panel 2i alignment workflow uses NGPhylogeny.fr (Lemoine et al., 2019,
[doi:10.1093/nar/gkz303](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkz303)), MAFFT (Katoh
and Standley, 2013, [doi:10.1093/molbev/mst010](https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/mst010)),
BMGE (Criscuolo and Gribaldo, 2010,
[doi:10.1186/1471-2148-10-210](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2148-10-210))
and MSAViewer (Yachdav et al., 2016,
[doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btw474](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btw474)).

# Exported analytical files

The standalone modules write editable SVG and PDF files, 300-dpi PNG previews,
and reusable R workspaces to `figures/generated/`. These files are linked below
when present.

```{r export-links, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
export_files <- c(
  "figures/generated/panel_A_phylogeny_radial_R_reconstruction.svg",
  "figures/generated/panel_A_phylogeny_radial_R_reconstruction.pdf",
  "figures/generated/panel_F_mature_miRNA_age_across_species.svg",
  "figures/generated/panel_F_mature_miRNA_age_across_species.pdf",
  "figures/generated/panel_G_miRNA_seed_age_no_human.svg",
  "figures/generated/panel_G_miRNA_seed_age_no_human.pdf",
  "figures/generated/Figure2H_human_methylation_age.svg",
  "figures/generated/Figure2H_human_methylation_age.pdf",
  "figures/generated/Figure2I_cg10501210_sequence_inventory.svg",
  "figures/generated/Figure2I_cg10501210_sequence_inventory.pdf",
  "figures/generated/Figure2J_methylation_macroclades.svg",
  "figures/generated/Figure2J_methylation_macroclades.pdf",
  "figures/generated/Figure2K_boreoeutheria_rank.svg",
  "figures/generated/Figure2K_boreoeutheria_rank.pdf",
  "figures/generated/figure2_plot_objects.rds",
  "figures/generated/figure2_workspace.RData"
)
export_files <- c(export_files,
  list.files("figures/supplementary_s2", pattern = "\\.(pdf|svg|rds|RData)$", full.names = TRUE),
  "reference/mir29_figure_02S_preprint_final.pdf")

available_exports <- export_files[file.exists(export_files)]
if (length(available_exports)) {
  cat(paste0("- [", basename(available_exports), "](", available_exports, ")\n"))
} else {
  cat("The export module did not report any files. Re-run the two standalone scripts and inspect `logs/`.\n")
}
```

# Reproducibility checks

```{r reproducibility-table, echo=FALSE}
check_objects <- list()
if (exists("figure2_mirna_checks")) {
  check_objects[["miRNA / phylogeny"]] <- figure2_mirna_checks
}
if (exists("figure2_methylation_checks")) {
  check_objects[["methylation"]] <- figure2_methylation_checks
}

if (length(check_objects)) {
  checks <- dplyr::bind_rows(check_objects, .id = "Module")
  knitr::kable(
    checks,
    caption = "Numerical safeguards for the portable Figure 2 workflow."
  )
}
knitr::kable(s2_checks, caption = "Numerical and layout safeguards for the approved S2 reconstruction.")
```

```{r source-manifests, echo=FALSE}
manifest_files <- c(
  "data/miRNA_phylogeny/input_manifest.tsv",
  "data/methylation/MANIFEST.tsv",
  "data/manual_and_alignment/provenance_manifest.tsv"
)
manifest_files <- manifest_files[file.exists(manifest_files)]

if (length(manifest_files)) {
  manifest_counts <- data.frame(
    Manifest = manifest_files,
    Records = vapply(
      manifest_files,
      function(path) max(0L, length(readLines(path, warn = FALSE)) - 1L),
      integer(1)
    )
  )
  knitr::kable(manifest_counts, caption = "Bundled provenance manifests.")
}
```
